description: The one player's rules that need no screen: what plays after an item ends, what the end does to the player, and how big the minimized player is. `op` says what a case checks. Ids are the ids of feed items (a video's id or a playlist's id; the two are treated alike here). `next`: what plays after an item ends. When an item is started from a page, the client keeps that page's list as it was then: `items`, the ids in the order shown, and `mode`, the watched chip's choice at that moment (unwatched, watched or all, shared/fixtures/feed-chips.json). Neither changes afterwards, whatever page or chip is showing when the item ends. `ended` is the id of the item that ended, `watched` the ids that are watched at the end (the ended one usually among them), and `autoplay` the `autoplay` setting at the end (shared/fixtures/settings.json). `expected` is the id that plays next, or null for none: the first id after `ended` in `items` that is not in `watched`. It is null when `autoplay` is false, when `mode` is watched, when `ended` is last or every later id is watched, and when `ended` is not in `items`. Ids before `ended` are never gone back to, and ids of `watched` that are not in `items` change nothing. `end`: what the end of an item does to the player. `place` is where the player is drawn: large (over the dimmed app), minimized (in the window's corner) or card (in place of its card's thumbnail). `next` says whether the `next` rule gave an item. `nextCardShowing` says whether the next item's card is on the page showing now; it is read only when `place` is card and `next` is true. `expected.kind` is next (the next item plays, in `expected.place`), stay (the player stays where it is, on the ended item) or close (the player is removed); `expected.place` is present only with next. The next item plays where the player is, except that a card whose next card is not on the page showing gives it to the minimized player. With nothing next, the large and the minimized player stay, stopped on the ended item until the user closes or expands them, and the card player closes. `minimizedSize`: the size of the minimized player's video. `viewWidth` is the window's inner width, and `expected` its `width` and `height`, all in the platform's layout units (CSS pixels, points, dp). The width is 356, or the window's width less a 16 margin each side when that is smaller, and never under 200; the height is the width × 9 / 16 rounded to the nearest whole number, and never under 200. So a window 388 wide or wider gets 356 by 200, and a narrower one is narrower and still 200 high.
